review_candidates.title: Technical Program Manager - CISO Office
review_candidates.description: In the Technology division, we leverage innovation to build the connections and capabilities that power our Firm, enabling our clients and colleagues to redefine markets and shape the future of our communities. This is a Technology Leadership & Strategy position at the Vice President level, which is part of the job family responsible for driving innovation, developing technology roadmaps, and providing vision and strategic direction to align technology initiatives with long-term business objectives, fostering a culture of excellence, growth and transformation across the organization. Morgan Stanley is an industry leader in financial services, known for mobilizing capital to help governments, corporations, institutions, and individuals around the world achieve their financial goals. Interested in joining a team that’s eager to create, innovate and make an impact on the world? Read on. This role is critical to sustaining and advancing executive-level reporting, business management, and governance activities across the Office of the CISO. The Vice President will own high-visibility cyber reporting processes, including the Cyber Executive Reporting Dashboard, board-level materials, senior stakeholder updates, and regional CISO engagement. The role will also support cyber finance and program management activities, helping translate complex cyber initiatives, risks, metrics, and financial information into clear, actionable insights for senior Technology, Finance, Cyber, and Risk stakeholders. The position requires seasoned judgment, strong delivery discipline, and the ability to manage sensitive, time-critical deliverables in a highly matrixed environment. The role is based in Baltimore to enable close collaboration with direct team members and the senior stakeholder community supported by the Office of the CISO. What You’ll Do In The Role Lead and manage executive cyber reporting deliverables for the Office of the CISO, including recurring senior management updates, board-level reporting, cyber education materials, and ad hoc stakeholder requests. Own the end-to-end operating model for the Cyber Executive Reporting Dashboard (CERD), including roadmap coordination, governance, data quality, enhancement prioritization, and alignment with source systems such as Jira and the Firm’s program management tool. Design enterprise Power BI dashboards and self-service reporting solutions in support of CISO Operations and required reporting. Partner with the reporting platform owner to develop complex DAX measures, KPIs, calculated columns, and reporting logic. Partner with initiative owners, Chiefs of Staff, Technology teams, Finance, Risk, and Cyber leadership to collect, validate, synthesize, and present cyber program information in a consistent, executive-ready format. Drive the continued maturation of cyber reporting processes, including dashboard enhancements, metric standardization, reporting cadence management, and automation opportunities across repeatable reporting and compliance activities. Support cyber finance business management activities, including budget tracking, financial reporting, headcount analysis, workforce and location planning inputs, and coordination across Technology Finance and cyber leadership stakeholders. Provide program and budget management support for key Office of the CISO priorities, ensuring deliverables are tracked, dependencies are managed, and risks or issues are escalated appropriately. Coordinate regional CISO engagement and reporting, including preparation of materials, stakeholder follow-up, input tracking, and alignment across regional and global cyber teams. Develop clear narratives, talking points, Q&A materials, and briefing documents for senior leaders to support internal governance forums, executive reviews, and external-facing discussions where appropriate. Manage cross-functional stakeholder engagement for cyber underwriting, risk reporting, governance, and strategic cyber initiatives, ensuring inputs are complete, deadlines are met, and messaging is aligned. Translate complex cyber, technology, risk, and financial information into concise executive-level materials that support decision-making and oversight. Maintain strong governance over reporting deliverables, including version control, source documentation, issue tracking, and recurring review cycles with senior stakeholders. Identify opportunities to improve reporting quality, reduce manual effort, and strengthen transparency across cyber performance, investment, delivery status, and risk posture. What You’ll Bring To The Role Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. 7+ years of relevant experience in business management, program management, cyber/technology reporting, financial management, risk management, or executive-level governance. Strong experience supporting senior executive stakeholders, with the ability to manage high-visibility deliverables, sensitive information, and competing priorities with sound judgment. Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional programs and coordinate across Technology, Finance, Cybersecurity, Risk, and business management teams. Experience with budget management, financial reporting, workforce/headcount analysis, program financials, or related business management activities. Strong understanding of management reporting disciplines, including data collection, quality control, metric development, reporting governance, and executive presentation development. Experience developing executive-ready materials, including dashboards, board presentations, senior leadership updates, briefing documents, talking points, and decision-support materials. Working knowledge of cybersecurity, technology risk, or information security concepts, with the ability to translate technical topics into business, operational, and risk-focused narratives. Power BI experience is required, along with familiarity with tools and processes such as Jira, PPM, Excel, and PowerPoint Familiarity with Agile delivery methodologies within a mature SDLC environment. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with the ability to connect details across programs, financials, risks, and stakeholder priorities. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to tailor messaging for executive, technical, financial, and risk audiences. High emotional intelligence, strong relationship management skills, and the ability to build trust with senior stakeholders in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. Proven ability to operate independently, manage ambiguity, prioritize effectively, and deliver polished work under tight timelines. Preferred Qualifications Experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk, operational resilience, or financial services technology. Experience supporting CISO, CIO, CTO, COO, Finance, Risk, or board-level reporting functions. Prior experience with cyber metrics, risk dashboards, governance forums, regulatory or audit-related reporting, or technology investment reporting. Familiarity with cybersecurity frameworks or risk concepts such as NIST CSF, CRI, ISO/IEC 27001 & 27002, SOC2, or similar governance and control frameworks. Experience identifying automation opportunities across reporting, compliance, financial management, or program governance processes. What You Can Expect From Morgan Stanley At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work. To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices into your browser. Expected base pay rates for the role will be between $125,000 and $175,000 per year at the commencement of employment. However, base pay if hired will be determined on an individualized basis and is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, incentive compensation, discretionary bonuses, other short and long-term incentive packages, and other Morgan Stanley sponsored benefit programs. Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. Our recruiting efforts reflect our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion, where individuals are hired, developed, and advanced based on their skills and talents. Our workforce reflects a broad cross-section of the global communities in which we operate, bringing a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives, and experiences. For more information, please visit: https://www.morganstanley.com/people-opportunities/eeo.
